record.paper_title: Open Problems in Partial Differential Equations Arising from Fluid Dynamics
record.original_question: Let a weak solution of the one-dimensional compressible Euler equations for a polytropic fluid arise as a vanishing-viscosity limit of the corresponding compressible Navier-Stokes equations as viscosity and heat conductivity go to zero. Must that limit be the unique entropy-admissible weak solution of the Euler Cauchy problem, or at least the unique weak solution obtainable as such a zero-dissipation limit?

evidence.quote: Uniqueness of the vanishing viscosity limits. Consider a weak solution to the one-dimensional Euler equations for polytropic fluids, which is a limit (in appropriate topology) of solutions of the corresponding Navier-Stokes equations as the dissipation parameters (viscosity and heat conduction coefficients) tend to zero.

Show that such a solution is the unique weak solution to the Cauchy problem for the Euler equations under appropriate entropy conditions. A less ambitious problem is to prove that such a solution is unique among the class of weak solutions which can be obtained as limit of solutions to the corresponding Navier-Stokes equations

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional compressible Euler equations governing a polytropic ideal gas:
  ρ_t + (ρ u)_x = 0,
  (ρ u)_t + (ρ u^2 + p)_x = 0,
  (ρ E)_t + (u(ρ E + p))_x = 0,
where ρ>0 is the density, u the velocity, E = e + u^2/2 the specific total energy, and the pressure obeys the polytropic law p = (γ−1) ρ e with adiabatic exponent γ>1, supplemented with initial data (ρ_0, u_0, e_0). Consider also the corresponding compressible Navier–Stokes system with viscosity coefficient μ>0 and heat conductivity κ>0:
  ρ_t + (ρ u)_x = 0,
  (ρ u)_t + (ρ u^2 + p)_x = μ u_{xx},
  (ρ E)_t + (u(ρ E + p))_x = (μ u u_x + κ θ_x)_x,
with the same initial data, where θ denotes absolute temperature linked to e by the polytropic constitutive relation.

Suppose (ρ, u, e) is a weak solution of the Euler Cauchy problem that arises as a limit, in some appropriate (e.g. distributional or L^p_{loc}) topology, of solutions (ρ^{μ,κ}, u^{μ,κ}, e^{μ,κ}) of the Navier–Stokes system as (μ, κ) → 0 along some sequence (with κ/μ in a physically reasonable range).

(a) Show that (ρ, u, e) is the unique entropy-admissible weak solution of the Euler Cauchy problem in a suitable admissible class.
(b) As a weaker assertion, show that (ρ, u, e) is unique within the class of weak solutions of the Euler Cauchy problem that can be realized as such a zero-dissipation limit of the compressible Navier–Stokes system.
artifact.category_tag: vanishing viscosity limit for compressible Euler
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature establishes existence of weak entropy solutions of the 1D compressible Euler equations for polytropic gases as vanishing-viscosity limits of Navier–Stokes systems (typically with density-dependent viscosity), via compensated compactness. However, no result asserts uniqueness of such limits as entropy-admissible weak solutions for general large initial data, nor uniqueness within the restricted class of zero-dissipation limits. The problem appears to remain open in both formulations.

status_evidence.title: Vanishing Viscosity Limit of the Navier-Stokes Equations to the Euler Equations for Compressible Fluid Flow with Vacuum
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of finite-energy entropy solutions of 1D compressible Euler for polytropic gases via vanishing viscosity from Navier–Stokes with density-dependent viscosity.
status_evidence.claim: Existence via inviscid limit is known, but uniqueness of the limit is not asserted.

status_evidence.title: Global Solutions of the One-Dimensional Compressible Euler Equations via the Inviscid Limit
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work continues to use the inviscid limit to construct solutions; uniqueness questions remain.
status_evidence.claim: State of the art focuses on existence, not uniqueness, of vanishing-viscosity limits.

status_evidence.title: Vanishing viscosity limit for the compressible Navier–Stokes system via measure-valued solutions
status_evidence.snippet: Limits obtained only in a measure-valued/weak sense, indicating non-uniqueness concerns persist.
status_evidence.claim: Available convergence is weak; uniqueness of the dissipative limit is unresolved.
